notes.title: Devblog #7: Picnic Area Pandemonium
notes.content:
[b]Night owls, I don’t know if I’m supposed to be furious or sad.[/b]

While you were enjoying that groovy tune, one of our park rangers called me. He told me that a bunch of no-good ruffians messed up the beautiful picnic area down near Granite Ridge. 

[h4]Tonight on KCKR, your community station for all things Ashwood Creek, we’ll talk about park etiquette, and how to behave in Ashwood Creek when you [b]DON’T want to be called out by the local radio host. [/b][/h4]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/b8888f2368f317197cb3f557d4053bebc51944ed.png[/img]


[b]Let me set the scene:[/b] Dirty picnic bench, trash everywhere. Music blaring from an abandoned boom box. An unsupervised fire. All of the above are[b] incredibly dangerous for our flora and fauna.[/b] And all of them were left on Granite Trail this morning. They even carved up some of our beautiful trees!

[b]Now, I hate pointing fingers[/b], but the mix of beer bottles, pop cans, and punk rock makes me think that the truants responsible for this mess are teenagers. This stuff has been happening for years. I remember one time, about 15 years ago, one of our park rangers complained about an eerily similar scene. History is a circle, I guess. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/07e93b72aec9c4da6726c23f6fc8c4cac7b7d473.png[/img]

Folks, I’m not going to pretend I’m a saint. I was young once. I was out and about all the time, partyin’. But I’ve learned a lot since then, so lemme give you some advice. The most important thing to remember is: [b]respect nature as much as you want it to respect you back[/b]. Think of other visitors, think of the plants, and think of the animals. You don’t want to rile those up. There’s bears roaming around in these parts…

But enough ranting.[b] I don’t want my blood sugar to go up even more.[/b] It’s a beautiful morning in Ashwood Creek. You’re listening to KCRK, and here’s another tune!

notes.title: Devblog #6: Investigating EVP
notes.content:
[b]Night owls, I’m shakin’ in my boots.[/b]

This morning, I was driving my grandson to school, when he told me about this rumour he’d heard from a friend. Folks, get this: apparently, the radios in Ashwood Creek are… [i][b]haunted! [/b][/i]

[h4]Now this is [b]KCKR, your community station for all things Ashwood Creek[/b], and usually we only get ghost stories from one of our callers. But this one was too interesting to pass up for an old radio veteran like me. [/h4]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/c79b12e71239e58ae370fbeabc34ac00da35a8ca.png[/img]

Here’s how the story goes: Someone’s walking ‘round the park at night, trying to tune their radio to a good channel. Maybe KCRK, maybe they’re trying to listen to the baseball game, who knows? They finally find a frequency and [b]everything starts goin’ crazy![/b] The radio’s glowing red, vibrating. And all of a sudden…[i] a creepy, distorted voice talking in riddles![/i] E.V.P., he called it. [i]Electronic voice phenomenon[/i]. Apparently, these things can even move things in the real world - opening doors, turning off lights, stuff like that. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/acb2124b638740265827c4bb37eca2edbd1e9237.png[/img]

Night owls, I don’t buy it. Scariest thing I’ve ever heard on the air was the Monster Mash! But I’d be curious to hear what you think. Is this bogus? And if not, what could it be? Ghosts? Extraterrestrials? Secret messages from a rogue network of spies? [b]Have you ever experienced an EVP?[/b]

Lines are open, I’ll be waiting for your calls.

notes.title: Radiolight: Post-Next Fest FAQ!
notes.content:
[h3]Hey everyone,[/h3]

Before we tune our radios back to our regularly scheduled programming, I wanted to use this opportunity to clear up a few questions that came up during Next Fest! A lot of you have been curious about the demo & game and I figured it’d make sense to have all the answers in one place. So, here goes nothing:

[b]How long will the demo be available?[/b]
Right now, the demo’s here to stay. That might still change, depending on how much the game will evolve as I keep working on it. But for now, you can enjoy the crisp night air of Ashwood Creek for as long as you want. 

[b]Will it be coming to consoles?[/b]
Development-wise, my full focus is on the PC release at the moment. If the launch goes well and there’s enough demand, I’d love to bring Radiolight to as many platforms as possible!

[b]What languages will the game be available in?[/b]
We’re proud to announce that, due to popular demand, Radiolight will include Spanish localisation at launch! That means that the game will be available in 6 languages, with original audio in English, and full interface localisation and subtitles in Czech, French, German, Simplified Chinese & Spanish. 

[b]Will it have controller support? [/b]
Yes! I’ll work hard to have full controller support at launch for Xbox, PlayStation and other controllers.

[b]So does that mean Steam Deck support at launch?![/b]
While the demo is already playable on Steam Deck if you tweak your control scheme a little, I will do my utmost best to have Steam Deck Verification at launch! However, even if we don’t have the highly coveted badge, I’ll test it and report how it runs before launch.
[b]
What about the music? Is it DMCA-free?[/b]
Radiolight’s score is a mix of licensed music and original tracks by Matheo Ramone, a talented young composer who uses synthesizers to bring the 80s mystery vibe to life. So far, I’ve only run into copyright issues with a couple of ambient tracks, but I'll look into how to fix that!

[b]How scary will the final game be?[/b]
Radiolight leans towards psychological horror, a thrilling experience with grim undertones, though there might be a few surprises. The goal is to create an unsettling atmosphere that sticks with you. So the answer is: just a little, but enough to feel fully immersed in the dark woods of Ashwood Creek.

[b]What’s the current focus of development?[/b]
Right now, I'm focusing on the events of the full game, including writing dialog and building out the final areas of the game. I’ve been reading your feedback and I'm working on tightening the environments and detailing them with more objects to find, along with other tweaks and improvements. I'm sure this will help me bring you the best version of Radiolight!

That's it for now! If you have any more questions, feel free to ask them in the comments below.

Time for me to head back to Ashwood Creek,
Krystof

notes.title: Thanks for Playing the Demo!
notes.content:
[h3]Hey hikers,[/h3]

[b]What. A. Week![/b] Steam Next Fest ended yesterday and having Radiolight be a part of it was an absolutely thrilling experience. I never expected that my little passion project would make such a big splash, and I’m [b]beyond grateful![/b]

I spent the entire week reading all of your posts & comments and watching your walkthroughs & streams. I want to thank each and every one of you for giving Radiolight a try.[b] Thanks for playing, thanks for sharing it with others, thanks for leaving reviews, and thanks for including me in your Best-of-Next-Fest lists! [/b]

Reading your feedback was super helpful, and I'm [b]working on addressing all the stuff that I feel like can make the game better based on your thoughts![/b] I know Next Fest is a lot. So many games, so little time to play (and replay) your favourite demos. [b]That’s why I decided to leave the Radiolight Demo up for now! [/b]If you haven’t had the time to play, or you’ve been meaning to show it to your friends, you can still do so.

All in all, this Next Fest was huge for Radiolight, and we’ve hit a bunch of milestones in the past week! The demo was [b]downloaded 10.000[/b] times and is currently sitting at a [b]97%[/b] positive rating on Steam. We’ve also hit [b]20.000 Wishlists[/b] on Radiolight, which I still have to pinch myself about a little bit. The impact of something like Next Fest for solo devs working on small games is immeasurable, and I couldn’t have done any of this without you! 

I was also stoked to see [b]so many creators cover the game on YouTube & Twitch[/b]. I tried to watch as much of your content as I could and it was an absolute pleasure to watch you play my game! There were so many fun videos out there - from [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V5O8Y7FHfDM]speedruns[/url] to some [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FxzCSkIiJsw]international creators[/url]  - and while I can’t share them all, here are some of my favourites:

notes.title: Radiolight: Demo - Live Now!
notes.content:
[h3]Hey everyone,[/h3]

[h4]Lace up your hiking boots & don’t forget to pack a few back-up batteries. It’s time for your[b] first-ever late-night stroll through Ashwood Creek National Park.[/b][/h4]

[b][h2]The Radiolight Demo is now live![/h2][/b]
[previewyoutube=uYdDyG4an1c;full][/previewyoutube]

In this demo, I’m giving you a first taste of the supernatural thriller I’ve been crafting – [b]you’ll get to step into the shoes of Ethan[/b] and explore a mysterious forest while searching for a park ranger named Harvey. All you’ll have is a [b]map, a flashlight, a walkie-talkie with your friend Robert on the other end, and an FM radio that’s been picking up strange signals. [/b]

[u][b]Are you ready to take your first steps into the world of Radiolight? [/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/22dcda73423e6d0d66bc734b0dfe0834faa2bb46.jpg[/img]
I’ve been thinking about this game for 7 years now, and reflecting on how far I’ve come is incredible. With Radiolight, I get to bring together everything I’m passionate about: a gripping investigative story, eerie 80s nostalgia, and a touch of the unsettling. Finally giving you a chance to play is truly electrifying and I can’t wait to hear your thoughts and theories. 

The demo is out now and you can play it through all of Steam Next Fest! If you get the chance to try it out, [b]please consider leaving a review on the demo page[/b]. It's the easiest way to help small games get more visibility on Steam!

[h4]Happy hiking,[/h4]

[b]Krystof Knesl[/b]
Solo developer of Radiolight

notes.title: Devblog #4: A Tribute to the Inspirations
notes.content:
[h3]Hey everyone,[/h3]

Slightly different blog, this time! [b]Krystof here[/b], interrupting our regularly scheduled radio program to delve into some of the media that inspired me to work on Radiolight. As a huge fan of [b]cinema, television and, of course, video games, I’m always looking for art that resonates with me.[/b]

Radiolight, at its core, is a deeply personal creation. It’s a game where you unravel mysteries, regrets, and fears, but it is also undeniably shaped by the many works that inspired me.

First and foremost, I want to mention [b]the surreal, haunting work of David Lynch[/b]. His ability to combine the unsettling & the serene and find terror in the ordinary was undoubtedly extraordinary – the cornerstone of Radiolight’s atmosphere. [b]I would like to thank him for what his art has brought to the world and pay tribute to his memory.[/b]

[previewyoutube=JPdZNCgIDek;full][/previewyoutube]

We can’t talk about inspirations, without mentioning the game that has become the figurehead of the Walking Sim genre. [b][i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/383870/Firewatch/]Firewatch[/url][/i], along with its gorgeous wilderness, captivated me by telling a story through a walkie-talkie[/b]. This direct connection between Henry & Delilah felt human and immediately struck me as a way to build characters even if they’re not currently present on screen.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d02lhvvVSy8

[b][i]True Detective[/i][/b] stands tall as another influence. Rust and Marty’s on-screen presence and dialogue were otherworldly, [b]bringing immense contrast to the ongoing investigation.[/b]

These are the most direct influences, but there are other echoes of inspiration. Some of them are subconscious: 
[list]
[*] [b]Stephen King[/b]’s stories come to mind, with their small-town horror. 
[*] [i][b]Stranger Things[/b][/i] with its unforgettable recreation of the 80s atmosphere. 
[*] [b]John Carpenter[/b]’s terrifying synth soundtracks. 
[/list]
Even the [b]Pacific Northwest itself, the setting of Radiolight, with its misty forests and isolated towns[/b] could be mentioned as an influence, drawing comparisons to [i][b]Twin Peaks[/b][/i] and [i][b][url=https://www.alanwake.com/]Alan Wake[/url][/b][/i].

It’s also been fascinating to hear what Radiolight reminds others of! Some have mentioned [i][b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/388880/Oxenfree/]Oxenfree[/url][/b][/i], [i][b]Silent Hill[/b][/i] and even games by [i][b][url=https://www.chillasart.co.jp/]Chilla's Art[/url][/b][/i].

Radiolight is a game shaped by my experiences and vision. It’s a chilling investigative experience, with all of these inspirations sprinkled throughout. I hope you’ll love it. I have something exciting to announce soon, so keep your eyes peeled!

notes.title: Devblog #3: The Park's Stunning Landmarks!
notes.content:
I can’t lie, night owls: I’ve put on a little bit of [i]weight over the holidays[/i]. And I imagine some of you have too. [b]Well, I can’t think of a better motivator than our beautiful national park! [/b]

[h4]Today on KCKR, your community station for all things Ashwood Creek, we’ll talk about some of the park’s landmarks that you can explore on your New Years Resolution hikes![/h4]

[u][h5]The Visitor Center[/h5][/u]

Whether you’ve hit the trails a thousand times or you’re just visiting the area as a little start-of-the-year treat, you should at least [b]pass by the Visitor Center[/b]. It’s the best way to learn about closed trails and weather conditions, [b]get in touch with any of our park rangers[/b], or go for a final, comfortable bathroom trip before you fully, [i]uh[/i], immerse yourself in nature... 

And don’t forget to [b]pick up a map on your way out! [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/b3cfda7f844fbbe31a591690decb787c178cb7cc.png[/img]

[h5][u]Granite Ridge[/u][/h5]

From the Visitor Center, you can move on to one of the park’s most stunning hiking areas: [b]Granite Ridge[/b]. Saunter along the Granite Trailhead as you can [b]feel the terrain slowly getting hillier & rockier[/b]. Get some rest & relaxation [b]at one of our picturesque picnic spots[/b] before you trek down the ridge’s mighty rock faces while the nearby creek whispers to-… 

[i]Sorry, I got a little poetic there[/i]. What I’m trying to say is: [b]Hike the Granite Trail. It’s really worth it. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/c36aa974f08f0aa6ab6d3372314ea874c9a1994e.png[/img]

[h5][u]The Ranger Cabin[/u][/h5]

Finally, I’ll let you in on a little insider info. Have you ever seen those little cabins strewn across the park? Those are for our Park Rangers![b] Whenever they need to rest for a bit or warm up in the colder months to do some work, they can just pop inside a cabin and light a fire – there’s even a bed! 
[/b]
So if you’re ever in an emergency, or just looking for a park ranger to help you out: the cabin is your best bet.

Listeners, there’s a lot of other stunning & interesting landmarks in Ashwood Creek National Park, but I’ll leave you with these for now. You can discover the depths of Misty Lake & the stunning vistas on Sentinel Lookout by [b]grabbing a map from the Visitor Center and just going on a little adventure. [/b]

Krystof

notes.title: Devblog #2: Things You’ll Need On Your Hike!
notes.content:
Night owls! I know we all like to spend our Sunday afternoons at the mall, but how ‘bout we don’t forget about [b]that stunning park[/b] that’s right on our front porch, huh? 

[h4]That’s right, everybody. This is KCRK, your community station for all things Ashwood Creek, and today we’re talking about hiking in our beautiful national park.[/h4]

As someone who’s deeply familiar with the trails of Ashwood, I can tell you: Hiking is for everybody! But you can’t just saunter out in your tennis shoes and hope for the best. Let me break down what you’ll need to [b]make it back from Granite Ridge and its surroundings safe & dry.[/b]

[h5][u][b]1. A Map of Ashwood Creek National Park [/b][/u][/h5]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/2109951f23e1fb74cadf9f9c769f989be1506fa0.png[/img]
Ashwood Creek is big and, no matter how much of your childhood you spent fishing & running around in the park, it’s better to be safe than sorry. The [b]park map is a handy visual aide that can help you navigate the stunning landmarks of the park and lead you to safety[/b] whenever you need it. Especially handy when going off-trail.

[h5][b][u]2. Light Up The Night[/u][/b][/h5]

Listeners, we all know you shouldn’t be in Ashwood Creek National Park after dark – but we also know that we’ve all done it. If you do decide to venture out after sundown, [b]please make sure to bring a flashlight[/b]. You’ll never know what obstacles and critters you’ll come across in the pitch black. Trust me, you want to be prepared when you choose to stay the night and witness the incredible sunrises we get here.

[h5][u][b]3. Emergency Broadcasts Are Your Friends[/b][/u][/h5]

Trust me, this is not just self-promotion. I already [i]know[/i] I’m your favourite radio host. But the trophy for Second Most Important Radio Broadcast in Ashwood Creek must go to the [b]Ashwood Creek Emergency Station[/b]. So don't forget to pack [b]an AM/FM radio[/b]! It’s the best way to stay up-to-date with any news from our steadfast crew of Park Rangers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/3daf852830d42752a73dcf5c811977167cec1940.png[/img]
[h5][u][b]4. Stay In Touch [/b][/u][/h5]

This one is for the thrillseekers out there. If you’re planning on rafting, bouldering, or going off-trail in general, it’s important to [b]stay in contact with the outside world[/b]. We already have a search party out there and we’d be happy to keep that number as low as possible. [b]If you’re scared of getting lost or injured, bring a Walkie Talkie![/b]

And if you take those precautions and wear a firm pair of boots, you should be good. Think I missed something? [b]Dial the station phone and tell me about your hike essentials.[/b] We’ll be taking calls after some smooth jazz, right here on KCRK Ashwood Creek. 

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

notes.title: Devblog #1: Tuning Into Ashwood Creek
notes.content:
[h3]Hello, night owls! You’re listening to KCRK - your community station for all things Ashwood Creek![/h3]

The air is crisp and cold tonight here in Ashwood Creek National Park, so I hope you’re all tucked into your coziest sleeping bags, inside one of our log cabins. 

Now, I’ve got a story for you that’s a little… [i]strange[/i]. You might want to turn up the volume on this one, because what we’ve got to share is more than just a bit of local news. It’s a story that’s unfolding right here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/ae2516fbfa20de0a0ce45e3b505f91f5efd9ca0e.png[/img]

You might’ve seen the poster of Elliot Laire - the young kid who’s gone missing right here in our beautiful park. While search efforts are still ongoing, we’ve just gotten reports that our very own park ranger Harvey has also been reported missing! But do not worry - Ashwood Creek’s police chief Robert has sent one of his best men into the park!

Now, we’re used to the usual quiet and serenity of our park, right? But for Ashwood Creek PD officer Ethan, that peace has been replaced with some downright eerie occurrences. Word around town is he’s been hearing things out there—shadows where they shouldn’t be, and some strange static coming through his radio. And no, it’s not just the usual tunes you’re used to hearing. It’s... different. Like someone—or something—might be listening in.

We don’t have all the details yet, but from what we’ve been hearing, things are getting pretty intense.

So, Ashwood Creek, here’s the question: What’s lurking out there, beyond the mist and the trees? Could it be something much darker than we ever imagined? Maybe my imagination is just drifting off into the night. 

But hey, if you’re out there listening tonight, just make sure your radio’s tuned in properly... You never know what might be out there, waiting to send you a signal.

Stay safe, and keep your eyes on the trees, folks. We’ll be here, keeping watch. You’re listening to KCRK!  

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

notes.title: Radiolight: Welcome to Ashwood Creek National Park
notes.content:
[h3]Hello hikers,[/h3]

Looking for your perfect destination for your next escape into the sprawling wilderness? Ashwood Creek National Park awaits! [b]Watch our brand-new promotional video below!
[/b]
[previewyoutube=FdzH34kPJ8Q;full]
[TRAILER LINK][/previewyoutube]
In Radiolight, you assume the role of Ethan, a police officer in the town of Ashwood Creek. You are drawn into your own past after [b]a local teenager goes missing[/b] under mysterious circumstances. 

Set in 1985,[b] this first-person narrative thriller, made by a solo dev,[/b] twists through foggy valleys and towering pines where secrets lie hidden beneath a seemingly tranquil surface. Guided by [b]strange interferences in the radio signal[/b], you delve deeper and deeper into the park. Navigating ghostly echoes of the past and uncovering the darkness that lies beneath Ashwood Creek.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39050852/9301912444326efbda0e27c1e6e439512612fa4a.png[/img]
[h5]A Message from Krystof Knesl[/h5] 
[b]Solo developer of Radiolight:[/b]

Radiolight began as a vision back in 2018 but I’ve always loved film and storytelling. [b]I grew up wanting to be a movie director, but I found my true passion in the immersive world of video games.[/b] Radiolight is my debut title, developed over four years. 

My goal was to craft an [b]intense, memorable experience that combines my favorite storytelling elements into a mind-bending narrative[/b] with gameplay that resonates deeply with players.

Over the coming months, I’ll be sharing some insights into the game and my dev process, so keep your eyes peeled for[b] some blogs and updates.[/b]

I can’t wait to take you all on this journey down [b]the winding trails of Ashwood Creek and the dark past of the police officer trying to uncover its mysteries. 
[/b]
Krystof
